subject: Foundation shortlist & parity-risk plan — next steps
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference>
To: Eva Torres <eva@finvault.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 16:12:00 -0800
Subject: Foundation shortlist & parity-risk plan — next steps

Hi Eva —

Thanks again for the demo today. Quick recap and a concrete plan for the evaluation phase so your team can move fast without losing alignment on parity/quality risks.

High-level ask from your side: validate that an open foundation model can match (or be near) your current proprietary baseline on the core customer support NLU + summary generation pipeline. Key constraints you mentioned: latency < 300ms p50 on our test infra, and no more than a 3-4% drop in customer-facing accuracy metrics for top intents.

Recommended shortlist (open models) for trial:
- OpenLlama-3-13B-v2 (quantized int8, recommended for throughput tests)
- Falcon-180B-Instruct-lite (fp16, for hardest summary prompts)
- Mistral-7B-Preview (fast, few-shot extraction tasks)

What we'll deliver to you by EOD tomorrow (attachments + links):
- Prompt bundle (prompt_bundle_v2.jsonl) mapped to your intent taxonomy
- Small benchmark harness with five gold test sets + scoring scripts (parity_benchmark_results.xlsx)
- Suggested rollout: canary trial on 2% traffic (FinVault staging) -> 25% -> 100% with automatic fallback to baseline on quality regressions

Proposed acceptance thresholds (we can dial these on the pilot):
- Task accuracy / intent F1: within 3% absolute of your proprietary baseline on core intents
- Summary ROUGE-L / semantic equivalence: no more than 5% degradation; prefer <3%
- Latency: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms on your staging infra
- Token-cost parity: target <1.4x current per-response cost (we'll show quantization tradeoffs)

Immediate next steps:
1) Please confirm which three test sets you want in the pilot (we attached our default five; happy to replace)
2) Confirm a start date for the canary week (we suggested Mon 2/21)
3) Provide the minimal connection details for staging (VPN jump host + workspace ID) or confirm if we should use a private-LT deployment

Attachments: finvault_model_spec_sheet.csv, parity_benchmark_results.xlsx, prompt_bundle_v2.jsonl, MAM_FinVault_v1.docx (mutual action plan)

Happy to jump on 20 minutes tomorrow to walk through the pilot timeline.

Thanks,
Sean

Subject: Re: Foundation shortlist & parity-risk plan — next steps

Thanks Sean — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying questions before we lock dates:

1) Acceptance thresholds: when you say "within 3% absolute" on intent F1, is that relative to baseline or absolute difference? Our product metrics are strict: for high-priority intents we need <=2% delta.
2) On the shortlist, which model would you recommend for extraction-heavy flows (entity normalization + canonicalization)?
3) For the privacy requirements, we need proof that KV caching and prefix caching won't persist data to shared hosts. Can you include a short security note?

We can start a canary on Mon 2/28 rather than 2/21 to give the security team time to review. If you can confirm the items above by EOW Friday, I can lock calendar time.

-Eva
Eva Torres

eva@finvault.com | +1 212-555-7890

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference>

Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.inference>
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 11:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Foundation shortlist & parity-risk plan — next steps

Hi Eva — quick answers inline and a suggested empirical acceptance plan we usually run for parity pilots.

On intent threshold: when Sean wrote "within 3% absolute" that was meant as absolute delta. That said, for your high-priority intents we will set a stricter gate: <=2% absolute delta. We'll codify per-intent gates in the MAM (attached).

Extraction-heavy flows: we recommend starting with Mistral-7B-Preview for entity extraction + normalization (few-shot extraction is strong and inference cost is lowest). If you see extraction accuracy hit but summaries lag, we add Falcon-180B-Instruct-lite for the summarization stage and route extraction->summary with policy-based routing. We can include both in the canary with traffic split (80% extraction to Mistral, 20% to fallback larger model) to measure end-to-end quality and cost impact.

Security / KV caching note: Redwood runtime never persists KV cache to disk in shared multi-tenant pools. For Private/VPC deployments we provide customer-only hosts and KMS-backed keys. We'll attach a one-page security note to the MAM and open a secure folder with SOC2 artifacts for your security team review.

Suggested empirical steps (our standard parity pilot):
- Baseline run: 2 full days of replayed traffic against your proprietary baseline to establish metrics
- Shortlist run: 2 days each per candidate model on the same traffic (same random seed / prompt ordering)
- A/B grading: human annotation on a stratified 1k sample comparing baseline vs open model on intent accuracy + summary fidelity
- Canary week: 7 days live on staging at 2% traffic with automated rollback if per-intent delta > gate for two consecutive days

Acceptance criteria we'll gate in the MAM:
- High-priority intents: <=2% absolute drop in intent F1 vs baseline
- Other intents: <=4% absolute drop
- Summary semantic equivalence: mean human score >= baseline - 4 points on our 10-point rubric
- Latency: p50 < 300ms, p95 < 800ms
- Cost: pilot cost estimate <=1.4x baseline (we'll show quantization options)

I'll attach a version of the MAM with these gates. If this looks good, Sean and Ben will kick off the harness and we'll provide the first benchmark CSV + scoring script by EOD Friday.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
